rv.q: Matthew Parker and his cast give it their all in a rough and ready production that displays considerably more dash than cash but boasts a fine central performance by Ian Hallard.

The great revelation in this European premiere of a penultimate play about the Bletchley codebreaker Alan Turing – given in the upstairs black box, once an actors’ bar, at the Arts – is how this apparent theatrical mayhem could be rigorously and satisfyingly structured.

cn.t: Snoo Wilson's imaginative play about Alan Turing receives mixed reviews, with critics praising the late playwright's surrealist vision and wide-ranging intellect while noting his challenging, unpredictable theatrical style.
